comments.body:
Thanks for picking up #3725. The diagnosis is right: `AlertPolicy` dedups on `(source, severity, message)` and ignores `data`, so a second subtask looping on the same tool never reached the model while the message named only the tool. Putting the subtask (and agent name) into the `LoopDetector` message, leaving the documented key unchanged, and correcting the docstring so it no longer suggests varying `data`, matches the bug.

The new test builds one loop alert per subtask, delivers the first, then applies both to a stateful policy. I expect `second[0]` to be the task-b prompt, because task-a's key is already in `_delivered_keys` and `apply` is called with an empty prompt list. I have not run the tests locally.

One non-blocking note: any other observer that followed the old docstring and relied on `data` to force a new delivery will still be collapsed. This PR's scope is `LoopDetector` plus the docs, which is the right fix for #3725.

— Jack Tan (@Jacktan007)

Thanks for reading through it. Agreed on the note: another observer that varies only `data` would still be collapsed, and this PR leaves the dedup key as documented. I also pushed a small test-only commit that fixes the two `arg-type` errors the type check reported in `test_delegated_events.py`; the remaining type and collection errors there are in `ag2/acp`, which this PR doesn't touch.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
